claims.text: The starting material is an equiatomic CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy.
Baseline CoCrFeNi exhibits low friction and wear at room temperature.
Baseline CoCrFeNi undergoes increased friction and accelerated wear at elevated temperatures, particularly above approximately 300–400 °C.
The elevated-temperature degradation of baseline CoCrFeNi is caused by uncontrolled oxide formation and tribochemical reactions.
The proposed intervention is addition of approximately 0.5 at.% Ti to CoCrFeNi.
A minor Ti addition will trigger in situ formation of a continuous protective oxide tribofilm during elevated-temperature sliding.
The proposed tribofilm will be thin, uniform, and adherent.
The tribofilm will contain Ti-rich oxides such as TiO2 or mixed spinel phases.
Ti will oxidize preferentially upon heating.
The Ti-containing oxide film will act as a self-lubricating layer.
The oxide film will minimize direct metal-to-metal contact and reduce interfacial shear forces.
The oxide film will suppress severe abrasion and adhesive wear by acting as a protective barrier.
Ti-modified CoCrFeNi will retain a lower and more stable coefficient of friction at elevated temperatures than unmodified CoCrFeNi.
Ti-modified CoCrFeNi will have a significantly lower wear rate near 800 °C than unmodified CoCrFeNi.
Ti-modified CoCrFeNi will maintain room-temperature friction behavior comparable to that of unmodified CoCrFeNi.
The intervention will maintain low friction and wear throughout approximately 25–800 °C.
The proposed operating boundary is dry sliding in ambient air near 1 N load and 0.1 m/s sliding speed over approximately 25–800 °C.

contradictions.description: The Ti content is stated as approximately 0.5 at.%, but the designation CoCrFeNiTi0.5 conventionally denotes a Ti molar coefficient of 0.5 relative to four unit-coefficient base elements, corresponding to about 11.1 at.% Ti rather than 0.5 at.%.
